name: Ayurvedic Treatment of Nephrotic Syndrome

sections.introduction:
People who don’t smoke, have proper body weight, eat healthy diet and are physically and mentally active they reduce their risk to various disorders. But in the era of modernization it is very difficult to maintain healthy lifestyle and healthy eating habits. Every person is too busy and everyone develop a world of materialistic wealth. We are ignoring this fact that we are living in world of serious environmental, social, physiological and psychological problems. We ignore the negative effects of our like style. Our static and comfortable lifestyle leads to various disease related to our renal function system, cardiac system, digestive system and reproductive system. 
 About Kidney Functions 
 Kidneys are bean shaped organ found in human body. Anatomical position of kidney is in back of abdomen. Size of each kidney is about 4-5 inch. Kidneys are very vital and functional organ found in our body. Essential function of kidneys is to purify blood. Blood passes through kidneys many times a day. It removes toxin and others wastes found in blood. Main function of kidneys is to maintain fluid and electrolyte balance. After the purification of body blood urine is resultant created by kidneys. After this urine collects in funnel shaped structure called pelvis. Then it is flushed to ureters and bladder. The whole procedure of purification to urination millions of nephrons are involved to complete this procedure. Nephrotic syndrome is group of symptoms that associated with renal system 

 About Nephrotic Syndrome 
 Nephrotic syndrome is group of various symptoms related to kidneys in which kidney excrete proteins in excess. In this syndrome protein level found in blood is decreased but cholesterol and trigylceride levels are vice versa (increased). Inflammation in kidneys is other major difficulty found in this disorder. In this syndrome small and tiny blood vessels called glomeruli are damaged and not able to filter toxins and wastes. 
 Ayurvedic Outlook 
 Ayurvedic term used for this disorder is “VRIKKA SHOTHA”. No particular cause is found for this disease. It is caused by autoimmune reactions and genetic causes. 
 According to Ayurveda MITHYA AHAAR VIHAAR is one major reason for this disorder. If we are taking wrong and unhealthy food for long time they imbalance pachak pitta in our body. Disturbed pachak pitta don not digest our food and produce large amount of unwanted materials in our body. These toxins are called AMA. 
 These toxins causes damage our kidneys and are responsible for causing nephrotic syndrome. 
 Classification of Nephrotic Syndrome 
 On the basis of causes nephrotic syndrome is divided into two types:- 

 Primary nephrotic syndrome 
 Secondary nephrotic syndrome 

 On the basis of histology nephrotic syndrome is distinguished into four following types:- 

 Minimal change disease 
 Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis 
 Membranous glomerulonephritis 
 Membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis 

 Causes of Nephrotic Syndrome 
 Primary causes 

 Hereditary nephropathy 
 Membranous nephropathy 
 Focal segmental glomeruloscleriosis 
 Minimal change disease 
 Diabetic nephropathy 

 Secondary causes 

 Genetic disorders 
 Immunity related disorders 
 Amyloidosis 
 Clot in kidney vein 
 Infections 
 Certain drugs 
 Cancer 

 Symptoms of Nephrotic Syndrome 
 Symptoms may include:- 

 Hyperprotinemia 
 Hyperlipidemia 
 Lipiduria 
 Hyponatermia 
 Puffy eyes 
 Swelling in feet and ankles 
 Pitting edema in legs 
 Excessive weight gain due to urine retention 
 Poor appetite 
 Seizures 

 Daignosis of Nephrotic Syndrome 

 Blood test 
 Urine test 
 Creatinine and creatinine clearance test 
 Kidney tissue sample test 

 Risk Factors of Nephrotic Syndrome 

 Medical conditions like diabetes, lupus and amyloidosis 
 Excess use of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs 
 Various infections like hepatitis c, hepatitis b, HIV. 

 Complications of Nephrotic Syndrome 

 Blood clots 
 Poor nutrition 
 Hypertension 
 Acute and chronic kidney failure 
 Renal vein thrombosis
